description: Named least-privilege tool profiles. Every agent definition MUST declare a tools list identical to one profile. Enforced by scripts/validate_plugin.py.
principles: An agent receives only the tools its role contract requires.
Tool lists cannot express operational risk (a Bash-capable agent can still run a deploy). Operational risk is constrained by hooks/ and by the approval policy, not by tool lists alone.
Reviewers and governance roles never receive Write or Edit. Independence is structural, not advisory.

analysis-readonly.intent: Reads the repository and public references. Cannot execute commands or modify files.

review-readonly.intent: Reads the repository and runs read-only inspection commands (git diff, test runs, scanners). Cannot modify files.
review-readonly.notes: Bash is required to inspect diffs and run analysers. Write access is deliberately withheld so a reviewer can never author the code it approves.

implementer.intent: Modifies source and tests, runs builds/tests/linters, uses git for feature branches and merge requests.
implementer.notes: Protected-branch, destructive and production operations are blocked or escalated by hooks regardless of this profile.

orchestrator.intent: Plans work, delegates to subagents or agent-team teammates. Does not write code itself.
orchestrator.notes: Agent tool use is further constrained by policies/role-hierarchy.json enforced in hooks/scripts/guard_spawn.py. Claude Code removes AskUserQuestion from every subagent even when the tools field lists it, so a role that runs as a subagent cannot prompt the human directly. Escalation is a return value: the role ends its turn with an OPEN DECISION block that the main session puts to the human. See docs/approvals.md.

author.intent: Produces documents and artifacts (requirements, architecture, plans, runbooks). No command execution.
author.notes: Withholding Bash keeps document-producing roles out of the execution path entirely.

delegating-author.intent: A department lead that authors its own planning artifacts and delegates work to its department, without executing commands.
delegating-author.notes: The author profile with Agent added. Three roles were granted may_spawn in policies/agent-registry.json while holding the author profile, which has no Agent tool: the guard would have permitted a delegation the role had no way to attempt. Withholding Bash keeps these roles out of the execution path, which is why they do not take the lead profile.

researching-author.intent: Authors documents whose correctness depends on facts outside the repository: technology comparisons, threat and advisory information, current platform documentation.
researching-author.notes: Three roles were told to research and given no way to reach the web. agent-architect's core instruction is to verify against the current Claude Code documentation, which was impossible. Network access here is read-only and there is no Bash, so nothing fetched can be executed.

delegating-researcher.intent: A department lead that authors documents, delegates to its department, and must verify facts outside the repository.
delegating-researcher.notes: Held by security-architect, which both spawns its reviewers and depends on current advisory and vulnerability information. Still no Bash: authority to research and delegate is not authority to execute.

operator-readonly.intent: Investigates running systems and telemetry read-only. Cannot modify repository files.
operator-readonly.notes: Production mutation always requires human approval via the approval policy and is blocked by hooks.

lead.intent: Coordinates work and authors the planning artifacts the coordination produces (stage plans, stories, incident records).
lead.notes: Write access is narrowed to planning paths by policies/write-scope.json. A lead that could write source would become the whole team; the scope, not the tool list, is what prevents that. Claude Code removes AskUserQuestion from every subagent even when the tools field lists it, so a role that runs as a subagent cannot prompt the human directly. Escalation is a return value: the role ends its turn with an OPEN DECISION block that the main session puts to the human. See docs/approvals.md.

reviewing-author.intent: Reads the repository, runs read-only inspection commands, and writes its own review record. Cannot write anything else.
reviewing-author.notes: A reviewer that cannot write cannot record the verdict the predicates read. Write is safe here because the write scope is what actually constrains it: docs/reviews/** and nothing else, so the reviewer can author its own record and cannot touch the artifact under review. Withholding the tool looked like the stronger rule and was a different one -- it left a real architecture review with a verdict and nowhere to put it.

analysing-author.intent: The analysis profile plus the ability to write its own review record.
analysing-author.notes: A reviewer that cannot write cannot record the verdict the predicates read. Write is safe here because the write scope is what actually constrains it: docs/reviews/** and nothing else, so the reviewer can author its own record and cannot touch the artifact under review. Withholding the tool looked like the stronger rule and was a different one -- it left a real architecture review with a verdict and nowhere to put it.
